title: Contrasting the Interaction Structure of an Email and a Telephone Corpus: A Machine Learning Approach to Annotation of Dialogue Function Units
abstract: Presents a dialogue annotation scheme applied to both a telephone transaction corpus and an Enron email corpus, representing interactions as Dialogue Function Units with explicit links between requests and responses. It trains classifiers to predict relations between unit pairs and permits unmatched requests, making it directly relevant to localized response scope in workplace email.

title: Detection of Question-Answer Pairs in Email Conversations
abstract: Develops methods for detecting questions and their corresponding answer segments in email threads. Thread-structure features improve question-answer pairing beyond lexical similarity, and the work explicitly motivates distinguishing questions about different issues and associating responses with the appropriate questions.

title: Question and Response Dynamics in Public Service Encounters
abstract: Provides more than 200 verbatim transcripts of authentic German conversations between street-level bureaucrats and citizens together with annotations of all question-response pairs. The study distinguishes response behavior including direct and more evasive responses in an authentic institutional setting.

title: ‘But what is the reason why you know such things?’: Question and response patterns in the LADO interview
abstract: Analyzes question-response pairs in five authentic institutional interviews. Directives frequently occur within multiple-question turns, and interviewees typically answer the most specific or most recent question rather than satisfying the accompanying directive, providing direct empirical evidence of partial response scope over multi-question antecedents.

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Reply-to Structures of Addressee Recognition
abstract: Models dialogue discourse structure by establishing discourse links and exploits addressee-recognition reply-to structures as a related source of structural supervision. A task-aware framework learns the shared and distinct structure of reply-to and discourse links on STAC and Molweni.

title: Structured Dialogue Discourse Parsing
abstract: Treats dialogue discourse parsing as finding discourse links and corresponding relations throughout multi-participant conversations. The method jointly optimizes structural links and relations and performs structured decoding rather than independently assigning local pairwise labels.

title: A Distance-Aware Multi-Task Framework for Conversational Discourse Parsing
abstract: Constructs utterance dependency structures for multi-party conversations while combining graph-based and transition-based parsing. The framework is specifically designed to improve both short- and long-distance discourse links, which is relevant when a response targets a non-adjacent antecedent.

title: Speaker-Aware Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Develops a discourse parser for multi-party dialogue that explicitly models interactions among speakers and predicts dialogue discourse structure. Speaker-context interaction and same-speaker pretraining improve structural link prediction on standard dialogue benchmarks.

title: Improving Multi-Party Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Domain Integration
abstract: Predicts dependency structures and discourse relations between elementary discourse units in multi-party conversations. It studies cross-domain generalization and domain integration for dialogue discourse-link prediction.

title: Dialogue Discourse Parsing as Generation: A Sequence-to-Sequence LLM-based Approach
abstract: Recasts dialogue discourse parsing as a text-to-text generation task so that a sequence-to-sequence language model generates discourse structures directly. The approach is evaluated on STAC and Molweni, where the target representation contains dialogue discourse links and relations.

title: Coherence-based Dialogue Discourse Structure Extraction using Open-Source Large Language Models
abstract: Investigates unsupervised extraction of discourse structures from multi-party dialogue by identifying coherent sub-dialogues. Dynamic-programming and greedy algorithms are evaluated on STAC and Molweni without requiring gold discourse attachments during training.

title: Enhancing Multi-party Dialogue Discourse Parsing with Explanation Generation
abstract: Combines LLM-generated explanatory information with structural parsing and contrastive learning for multi-party dialogue discourse parsing. The model targets discourse structure rather than merely classifying the current utterance and is evaluated on STAC and Molweni.

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing through Discourse-aware Utterance Clarification
abstract: Introduces a clarification module that reasons about ambiguous dialogue utterances before discourse parsing, including reasoning about the intended discourse relation. The parser evaluates whether clarifications improve structural predictions and is tested on STAC and Molweni.

title: An Annotation Scheme of A Large-scale Multi-party Dialogues Dataset for Discourse Parsing and Machine Comprehension
abstract: Proposes an annotation scheme for large-scale multi-party Ubuntu chats containing explicit discourse structure together with question-answer information. The representation supplies discourse links among conversational units rather than only message-level reply structure.

title: Molweni: A Challenge Multiparty Dialogue-based Machine Reading Comprehension Dataset with Discourse Structure
abstract: Provides a large multiparty-dialogue corpus with discourse dependency annotations in an SDRT-style representation. It also includes answerable and unanswerable reading-comprehension questions, while the discourse annotations support explicit conversational attachment modeling.

title: A Joint Model for Dropped Pronoun Recovery and Conversational Discourse Parsing in Chinese Conversational Speech
abstract: Jointly models dropped-pronoun recovery and conversational discourse parsing. Its discourse component constructs a conversational discourse graph with a biaffine link predictor, supplying transferable machinery for antecedent-link discovery in dialogue.

title: Discourse Dependency Structures as Constrained DAGs
Toward Dialogue Modeling: A Semantic Annotation Scheme for Questions and Answers
abstract: Proposes detailed annotations for both the semantic content and discourse contribution of question-answer pairs. The scheme is applied to dialogues in English, Spanish, and Dutch and is accompanied by initial automatic-annotation experiments.

title: Characterizing the Response Space of Questions: a Corpus Study for English and Polish
abstract: Develops a fine-grained taxonomy intended to cover the full response space of questions rather than only direct answers. The taxonomy is grounded in corpus studies of English dialogue corpora and compared with Polish conversational data.

title: Characterizing the Response Space of Questions: data and theory
abstract: Extends a corpus-grounded taxonomy to cover diverse responses to questions across several dialogue corpora and languages. It reports annotation reliability and formalizes response classes in a dialogical semantics, providing empirical distinctions beyond simple answer/non-answer labels.

title: UgChDial: A Uyghur Chat-based Dialogue Corpus for Response Space Classification
abstract: Introduces two-party and multi-party chat data containing explicitly identified question-response pairs. The pairs are annotated using a fine-grained response-space taxonomy, providing chat-based empirical evidence about different ways a question can be responded to.

title: A corpus-based taxonomy of question responses
abstract: Uses corpus evidence to develop a taxonomy of responses to questions rather than treating all following turns as equivalent answers. The taxonomy is intended to support formal and computational models of dialogue response behavior.

title: Query responses
abstract: Presents a large-scale corpus study of cases where a query is answered with another query. It develops a response taxonomy and shows that response categories differ in how often a subsequent answer is eventually provided, offering evidence for tracking unresolved questions across turns.

title: Answering Clarification Questions
abstract: Investigates clarification questions and their answers using corpus and experimental evidence. It examines relationships among clarification-request type, whether and how the clarification is answered, and the distance between request and answer.

title: Asking between the lines: Elicitation of evoked questions in text
abstract: Introduces a scalable method for eliciting Questions Under Discussion from naturalistic discourse and subsequently determining which elicited questions become answered as the discourse continues. This provides transferable annotation machinery for explicit unresolved-question tracking.

title: Discourse Analysis via Questions and Answers: Parsing Dependency Structures of Questions Under Discussion
abstract: Builds a QUD parser that derives dependency structures over full documents, treating later sentences as answers to questions evoked by preceding context. The approach is transferable to proposition-level antecedent discovery because the question itself represents the relation connecting a response to prior discourse.

title: Towards automatically generating Questions under Discussion to link information and discourse structure
abstract: Automates part of QUD annotation by generating potentially relevant questions for assertions in authentic discourse. The work is explicitly designed to link information structure with discourse structure and therefore supplies transferable machinery for representing proposition-to-question dependencies.

title: Inferring Acceptance and Rejection in Dialogue by Default Rules of Inference
abstract: Analyzes how dialogue participants infer whether assertions and proposals have been accepted or rejected. The account combines logical consistency, information structure and prosody, and develops a common-ground model covering several forms of acceptance and rejection.

title: Identifying Agreement and Disagreement in Conversational Speech: Use of Bayesian Networks to Model Pragmatic Dependencies
abstract: First identifies adjacency pairs by ranking candidate utterance pairs using lexical, durational and structural features, and then classifies the linked pair as agreement or disagreement. Because antecedent-pair discovery precedes stance classification, the work directly addresses agreement/disagreement target selection rather than assuming a fixed target.

title: Conversational Grounding: Annotation and Analysis of Grounding Acts and Grounding Units
abstract: Annotates two dialogue corpora with Grounding Acts, Grounding Units and degree of grounding. Grounding Units explicitly organize sequences of conversational acts involved in establishing shared understanding, providing a structured representation relevant to acceptance and response scope.

title: A "speech acts" approach to grounding in conversation
abstract: Models grounding as actions performed by conversational participants to establish mutual understanding. It defines Grounding Acts and a grammar specifying sequences of such acts that result in content becoming grounded.

title: Contributing to discourse
abstract: Argues that discourse contributions require interlocutors to establish mutual belief that an utterance has been understood sufficiently for current purposes. It develops conversational contribution units and a collaborative account of how material enters common ground.

title: Opening Up Closings
abstract: Provides a foundational conversation-analytic study of how conversational sequences are organized and brought to closure. Its analysis of sequential organization helped establish the interactional framework from which adjacency-pair and conditional-relevance accounts of responses developed.

title: Discourse Deixis: Reference to Discourse Segments
abstract: Develops an account of discourse-deictic reference in which expressions can refer to portions of prior discourse and to discourse-model objects evoked by those segments. It is foundational for treating antecedents as discourse segments rather than only nominal entities.

title: Resolving Individual and Abstract Anaphora in Texts and Dialogues
Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project
abstract: Extends an anaphora annotation scheme to abstract anaphora whose antecedents can be verbal phrases, clauses and discourse segments. Inter-annotator results on texts and dialogues in Danish and Italian indicate that these abstract-antecedent distinctions can be annotated reliably.

title: The DAD Parallel Corpora and their Uses
abstract: Describes abstract-anaphora annotations in parallel and comparable written and spoken corpora. Antecedents include verbal phrases, clauses and discourse segments, while the referenced abstract objects include events, situations and propositions; the paper also reports machine-learning experiments on the annotations.

title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
abstract: Introduces an anaphorically annotated corpus that explicitly represents multiple antecedents for ambiguous anaphoric expressions and discourse antecedents for references to abstract entities such as events, actions and plans. Its genres include task-oriented dialogues, making the representation especially relevant to ambiguity and multiple valid antecedents.

title: Resolving abstract anaphors in Spanish discourse: Underspecification and mereological structures
abstract: Studies abstract anaphora where candidate antecedents are clauses, sentences and larger discourse fragments and the ambiguity occurs at the propositional level. It proposes constructing a complex abstract object with a mereological structure so that an anaphor can resolve to an atomic proposition or to a merged interpretation of multiple thematically connected propositions.

title: Scoring Coreference Chains with Split-Antecedent Anaphors
abstract: Generalizes coreference evaluation metrics to references whose interpretation is constructed from multiple antecedents. The scoring approach has been applied both to split-antecedent plural references and to discourse deixis in dialogue, providing evaluation machinery for genuine multi-antecedent structures.
